articles.title: Rebels kill 15 in South Sudan
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: An official hinted at fighters loyal to the country's former first Vice-President Riek Machar, a longtime rival of President Salva Kiir who has been under house arrest since March 2025
An attack on Sunday (November 22, 2026) by rebels in northwestern South Sudan has killed at least 15 civilians, with the toll likely to rise, local sources told AFP .
One official pointed the finger at fighters loyal to the country's former first Vice-President Riek Machar, a longtime rival of President Salva Kiir who has been under house arrest since March 2025.

“The attack on the Bol Bol Boma area in Tonj East County, Warrap State, began late on Saturday,” Machuei Bith, the county's caretaker commissioner, told AFP . He blamed the deaths on fighters from neighbouring Unity State belonging to Machar's SPLA-IO armed group.

"Fifteen civilians and cattle keepers were killed and four armed attackers with SPLA-IO uniforms were also killed," he told AFP . A local police officer confirmed the story on condition of anonymity and said the fighting was still ongoing on Sunday morning. "Further details on casualties from both sides will be shared later on with the media," the officer said.
23 dead in clashes between South Sudan government, opposition forces

Since independence from Sudan in 2011, the world's youngest country has been forced to grapple with various violent conflicts, linked to political infighting, ethnic tensions or competition for resources.
Between 2013 and 2018, the eastern African country was torn apart by a civil war pitting forces loyal to Machar against those supporting Kiir, which left more than 4,00,000 people dead.

An attack on Sunday (November 22, 2026) by rebels in northwestern South Sudan has killed at least 15 civilians, with the toll likely to rise, local sources told AFP .

One official pointed the finger at fighters loyal to the country's former first Vice-President Riek Machar, a longtime rival of President Salva Kiir who has been under house arrest since March 2025.

“The attack on the Bol Bol Boma area in Tonj East County, Warrap State, began late on Saturday,” Machuei Bith, the county's caretaker commissioner, told AFP . He blamed the deaths on fighters from neighbouring Unity State belonging to Machar's SPLA-IO armed group.

"Fifteen civilians and cattle keepers were killed and four armed attackers with SPLA-IO uniforms were also killed," he told AFP . A local police officer confirmed the story on condition of anonymity and said the fighting was still ongoing on Sunday morning. "Further details on casualties from both sides will be shared later on with the media," the officer said.

23 dead in clashes between South Sudan government, opposition forces

Since independence from Sudan in 2011, the world's youngest country has been forced to grapple with various violent conflicts, linked to political infighting, ethnic tensions or competition for resources.

Between 2013 and 2018, the eastern African country was torn apart by a civil war pitting forces loyal to Machar against those supporting Kiir, which left more than 4,00,000 people dead.

articles.title: India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 16
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during PM Modi's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force in 2027

India and the 27-nation bloc European Union (EU) are likely to sign the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) on December 16, an official said. The two sides concluded the negotiations for the pact on January 27 this year.

European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force next year.

The European Commission has already submitted proposals to the Council of the European Union seeking authorisation for signing and conclusion of the agreement, along with the final legal text and tariff schedules.

Under the free trade agreement, described as 'mother of all deals', 93 per cent of Indian shipments will enjoy duty-free access to the 27-nation bloc, while imports of luxury cars and wines from the EU will become less expensive.

The deal, concluded after negotiations spanning over two decades, will create a market of about 2 billion people across the world's fourth-largest economy, India, and the second-largest economic bloc, the EU.

Taken together, India and the EU account for 25% of global GDP and one-third (about USD 11 trillion) of international trade (about $33 trillion).
The EU is India's largest trading partner in goods among individual blocs, while India ranks as the EU's ninth-largest goods trading partner globally and sixth in services.

articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears.

Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026.
Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor.
“We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district.

Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia.

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.”

The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”

“Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia.

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.”

The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”

“Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

articles.title: Health Wrap Episode 60 discusses healthcare spending, antimicrobial resistance and more
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The episode discuss trends in healthcare expenditure in India, concerns over the regulation of fertility services, the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance, and the impact of environmental and social conditions on public health

The 60th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu looks at key developments in public including healthcare financing, reproductive health, antimicrobial resistance, tuberculosis, environmental exposures and diabetes care.

Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, and Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu, discuss the latest National Health Accounts estimates for 2023–24, which show a substantial increase in government health expenditure and a decline in the share of household out-of-pocket spending nationally. The episode also examines the contrasting trends in Keralam, where household healthcare expenditure has increased and the share of government spending has declined.

The episode looks at the drug regulator’s direction to pharmaceutical companies to comply with revised prices for 137 anti-cancer drugs and the potential implications for treatment costs. It also examines concerns over an illegal human egg collection racket in Telangana, including questions about informed consent, women’s safety and the regulation of assisted reproductive technology centres. Developments in Karnataka’s proposed mid-life women’s health programme and mandatory gynaecological check-ups for girls are also discussed.

Marking World AMR Awareness Week, the episode explores the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance and the need for appropriate antibiotic use, timely diagnosis, infection prevention and surveillance. It also discusses phage therapy, which uses bacteriophages to target bacterial infections, and its potential role in addressing infections that do not respond to conventional antibiotics.

The discussion also examines tuberculosis through the lens of social and economic vulnerability, highlighting the importance of nutrition, housing and social support alongside diagnosis and treatment. It looks at the latest figures on domestic funding for India’s TB response, which now accounts for 86% of total spending, even as external funding declines.

The discussion also examines the health risks of extreme heat for pregnant women and newborns. A survey of healthcare professionals across five countries found that 98% of Indian clinicians surveyed had treated pregnant women and newborns whose health they believed had been affected by extreme heat.

The episode also looks into how fear of diagnosis may discourage people from screening and discusses a Chennai initiative that uses dietary counselling by staff nurses to improve blood sugar control and support long-term diabetes management.
The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: One country, hundreds of dal recipes: exploring India’s diverse lentil traditions
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A look at how the humble ingredient travels through different soils, histories, cultures, climates, and kitchens

From Rajasthan in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, from Kashmir in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, India does dal in thousands of ways. There are no fixed proportions to what comes to the table, and everyone’s mother’s recipe is just right. From mamidikaya pappu , or mango dal , to palak dal and dal makhani , there is great diversity in how lentils are prepared across the country. Dal’s resonance here goes beyond the fact that India is the world’s largest producer and consumer of pulses: it is often a reminder of home, a longing for the simple things in life, and a connector of cultures.

That intimacy with dal , however, does not mean everyone makes it the same way — or even that home is where it tastes best. For Harpreet Singh, 26, the dal he cooks at the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) is far better than what is cooked at home. “It’s the ghee that makes the difference,” he says with a laugh, adding that at home, it is rationed. At the temple, five kilos of ghee are added to a quintal of dal . “But the real secret is that we add sarson ka tel [mustard oil] once the dal is boiled, after the mail [froth] on top has been skimmed off,” he says.

Singh’s companion cook adds that it is also the pre-dawn prayers that go into the degchis (wide-mouthed cooking pots) , some of which can hold up to four quintals of dal , which also takes 100 kg of onion, 24 kg of salt, 16 kg of ginger and garlic each, 6 kg of turmeric powder, and 5 kg of khada masala (whole spices). The gurbani (reading of the scriptures) plays on a loudspeaker through the kitchens and service area.

Amritsar’s Golden Temple feeds 70,000 to 80,000 people on weekdays, with the number going to over a lakh on special weekends like amavasya (new moon), and up to 2.5 lakh on a guru’s birthday. In the kitchen, three shifts of about 450 people cook 15-20 quintals of dal daily, over wood-fired stoves. The most popular dal dish here is the mixed variety, which is boiled for six hours. In the langar , a free communal dining hall spread across several rooms and capable of seating 3,000 people at a time, dal is a staple. “Everyone is happy eating it,” says Singh, adding that people also pack food in vessels for patients in hospitals.

From former India cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur’s fondness for dal and rice while playing for India, to Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra bringing her home-cooked dal and bhindi to Parliament, and the slow-cooked, indulgent Dal Raisina served at Rashtrapati Bhavan, dal cuts across social and culinary divides. It is one of India’s most unassuming yet enduring staples — everyday comfort food that can be as humble or elaborate as the occasion demands.

Dal’s resonance here goes beyond the fact that India is the world’s largest producer and consumer of pulses: it is often a reminder of home, a longing for the simple things in life, and a connector of cultures.

That intimacy with dal , however, does not mean everyone makes it the same way — or even that home is where it tastes best. For Harpreet Singh, 26, the dal he cooks at the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) is far better than what is cooked at home. “It’s the ghee that makes the difference,” he says with a laugh, adding that at home, it is rationed. At the temple, five kilos of ghee are added to a quintal of dal . “But the real secret is that we add sarson ka tel [mustard oil] once the dal is boiled, after the mail [froth] on top has been skimmed off,” he says.

Singh’s companion cook adds that it is also the pre-dawn prayers that go into the degchis (wide-mouthed cooking pots) , some of which can hold up to four quintals of dal , which also takes 100 kg of onion, 24 kg of salt, 16 kg of ginger and garlic each, 6 kg of turmeric powder, and 5 kg of khada masala (whole spices). The gurbani (reading of the scriptures) plays on a loudspeaker through the kitchens and service area.

Amritsar’s Golden Temple feeds 70,000 to 80,000 people on weekdays, with the number going to over a lakh on special weekends like amavasya (new moon), and up to 2.5 lakh on a guru’s birthday. In the kitchen, three shifts of about 450 people cook 15-20 quintals of dal daily, over wood-fired stoves. The most popular dal dish here is the mixed variety, which is boiled for six hours. In the langar , a free communal dining hall spread across several rooms and capable of seating 3,000 people at a time, dal is a staple. “Everyone is happy eating it,” says Singh, adding that people also pack food in vessels for patients in hospitals.

From former India cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur’s fondness for dal and rice while playing for India, to Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra bringing her home-cooked dal and bhindi to Parliament, and the slow-cooked, indulgent Dal Raisina served at Rashtrapati Bhavan, dal cuts across social and culinary divides. It is one of India’s most unassuming yet enduring staples — everyday comfort food that can be as humble or elaborate as the occasion demands.

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery.

It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary.

“The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said.

“While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added.
He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December.
“The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted.
‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

fullParagraphs: Likud laid down conditions for a unity government, including no Arab parties and rejection of a Palestinian state, while Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government

The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over whether to form a coalition government, with Mr. Netanyahu’s party insisting on keeping his main policies.

Delegations from Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud began their meeting at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

A former Chief of Staff of the army, Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6, 2026, to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the October 2026 elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.

His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.
Mr. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel.

Such an arrangement could allow him to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023.

But that prospect runs up against Mr. Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Mr. Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. His ally, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, also reiterated on Saturday (November 21, 2026) his refusal to join a coalition with “Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances”.

On Saturday (November 21, 2026), Yashar presented the resumption of talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying Mr. Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Mr. Netanyahu.

Among other things, it demands an end to “all personal attacks and incitement to hatred” targeting the outgoing Prime Minister and his government. It also called for bringing together “all the parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people”, without the participation of Arab parties. Mr. Netanyahu and his allies regularly target Arab parties, which secured a record 19 seats in the legislature and are opposed to his remaining in power.

Likud is also demanding agreement on several major policy positions, notably rejecting the creation of a Palestinian state, maintaining Israeli control over territories in Syria, Lebanon and the Gaza Strip, and a compromise on conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jews, a particularly sensitive issue in Israel.

articles.title: Ex-U.K. PM Theresa May tells successor to ‘move on’ from Brexit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Former British Prime Minister Theresa May said she was “aghast” that Prime Minister Andy Burnham could be considering rejoining the European Union, after he sealed trade and youth mobility deals in Brussels

Ms. May’s remarks came after Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU’s top officials on Friday (November 20, 2026) sealed deals at a Brussels summit to ease trade and youth mobility. A decade after Britain narrowly voted to leave the bloc, Mr. Burnham has re-energised talk of closer ties ahead of a government 10-year plan for the U.K., set to be unveiled next month.

Ms. May warned that negotiations with the EU risked taking up vast amounts of government time, hampering efforts to tackle other issues. “And that’s one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU,” she said.

Ms. May, who supported remaining in the 27-member bloc, said government had to respect the result of the 2016 referendum. “When I became prime minister, I was very clear. People have voted for Brexit. We should deliver Brexit,” she told BBC television.

“He (Burnham) wants to pat them (voters) on their head and say ‘you know what? Remember that vote? Well you got it wrong, didn’t you? So have another go and come up with the right answer’,” she said. Ms. May was forced to quit in May 2019 after failing to get her Brexit deal through parliament.

“My message to him (Burnham) really is: People voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on,” she added. Mr. Burnham, who has been in office since July 2026, has committed to his predecessor Keir Starmer’s “red lines” on Europe for this parliament, meaning no return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement. But pro-Brexit campaigners fear he will push at some point to rejoin the 27-nation grouping.
Europe Minister Hamish Falconer said the world had changed since 2016, and the U.K. needed to “think over the long term about our relationship with Europe”.

“That’s why the prime minister is going to set out more next month as part of the 10-year plan about the long-term relationship between the UK and the EU,” he told Sky News . But he insisted the British people “are going to be the boss of every stage of this”.
“We are talking, as the prime minister was clear, about the long term. We will have a general election before then. People will be able to express their views,” he said.
Following Mr. Burnham’s EU deals, legislation to allow the U.K. to align with certain EU rules, including on food standards, is due to be introduced in parliament this week.

articles.title: Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry is in its early stages, U.S. media reported, after Jensen Huang’s resignation as chief executive and a 14% fall in Nvidia shares on Friday (November 20, 2026)

U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported on Saturday (November 21, 2026), citing people briefed on the confidential investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported on the investigation earlier this week, although it was unable to establish its precise focus. The probe could end without any charges being brought against the company.

Questions about Nvidia’s financial disclosures have intensified amid scrutiny of its dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company investigated by American authorities over suspected shipments of restricted AI chips to China. articles.title: Iran strike wounds two in Bahrain, Riyadh denounces ‘criminal’ attacks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Bahrain said two people were wounded in an attack on “a civilian industrial site”, while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted U.S. air defence systems.

Bahrain on Sunday (November 22, 2026) said two people were wounded in an Iranian attack on Saturday (November 21, 2026) against “a civilian industrial site” in the kingdom, which has repeatedly come under attack in recent days.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards have repeatedly said they targeted U.S. facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed on November 13 after a lull since early September.
“In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain... a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded,” Bahrain’s Interior Ministry said on X.

Two residents told AFP they had seen smoke rising above Sitra Island, east of Manama, which hosts several industrial facilities, including a refinery operated by the state-owned oil company Bapco.

In a statement carried by Iranian state media on Saturday evening, the Revolutionary Guards said they had attacked with missiles and drones U.S. Patriot air defence systems at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, in response to the “continued violations of the airspace” of the Islamic Republic.
Tehran said on Saturday it had intercepted a U.S. drone targeting Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic maritime corridor at the heart of the war in West Asia.

Bahrain’s powerful neighbour Saudi Arabia on Sunday lambasted Tehran for its continued “brutal aggression” against Gulf countries. In a statement published on X, the Saudi Foreign Ministry expressed “the strongest condemnation and denunciation by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia of the criminal Iranian attacks against a civilian industrial facility in the brotherly Kingdom of Bahrain”.

Saudi Arabia also announced early on Sunday that it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis in the west of the kingdom. The region is home to key energy infrastructure, including the oil terminal at the port of Yanbu, as well as the Jizan refinery, located in the far southwest of the country, near the border with Yemen.

articles.title: COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries.

On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.”

“We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties.

Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”.

“Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 22 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries.

On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.”

“We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties.

Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”.

“Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

articles.title: Drone strikes hit homes, UN premises in Sudan's capital
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia
“Drones struck Sudan 's capital Khartoum, damaging residential homes and a United Nations building on Sunday (November 22, 2026),” witnesses and the world organisation said.

Explosions were heard in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from at around 2 a.m. until approximately 4:30 a.m. (0000-0230 GMT). A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia.

"The drone attack at dawn today is a continuation of Ethiopian aggression against Sudanese territory, as the drones were launched from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport," the source told AFP . Sudan has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of allowing attacks to be launched from its territory, a claim Addis Ababa has denied.

Another witness reported that a drone hit the home of a mosque's muezzin, the person who calls Muslims to prayer, in Jebel Aulia, around 45 km (28 miles) south of Khartoum. "People were trying to rescue family members trapped under the rubble," the witness added.

The UN meanwhile said that "a UN premises with UN colleagues in the building was damaged". "This occurred in a civilian neighbourhood," the UN's Humanitarian Office (OCHA) said in a statement posted on X.
OCHA condemned the risk posed to humanitarian workers, saying it was "unacceptable" that UN personnel were being exposed to such danger. Authorities did not immediately report on casualties.

The conflict, which erupted in April 2023 between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Army, has killed more than 2,00,000 people, aid workers estimate, and triggered the world's largest hunger and displacement crises.
The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides' rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026.

“Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes,” the UN said last week. A Sudanese Army drone strike killed 15 people, including four children, in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the Army pushed through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.

The rival forces have for the last year wrestled for control of the resource-rich southern Kordofan region, which connects the Army-held centre and east to RSF-controlled Darfur. In recent months, both the Army and the RSF have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.

fullParagraphs: Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and reduced administrative burdens

articles.title: Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practise successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

articles.title: Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.

As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.

As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears.

Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026.
Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor.
“We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district.

Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.
Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care

articles.title: Digital planetariums, education centres will be established in all divisions: Bihar Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Requisition for appointment of 1,061 faculty posts for Engineering Colleges and 354 faculty posts for polytechnic colleges sent to BPSC

With a view to developing a scientific temperament among students and the general public, state-of-the-art “digital planetariums and education centres” will be established in all the divisions of the state, Bihar Science and Technology Minister Sheela Kumari said on Friday (November 20, 2026).
“The district magistrates of the districts concerned have been requested to provide a minimum of two acres of land for the purpose,” Ms. Kumari said while addressing a press conference in Patna.

These centres will provide children and young people with practical knowledge of astronomy and space research, she said, while praising Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary’s leadership for the initiative.
In reply to a query, she said that these planetariums will be ready in a year.

The Minister further stated that digital planetariums/space and astronomy education centres will also be established in three districts—East Champaran, Jamui, and Purnea—as part of the Union Ministry of Culture’s Scheme for Promotion of Culture and Science (SPOCS).

“The total estimated project cost is ₹39.00 crore, which will be funded with central assistance,” she said, adding that the target is to commence construction work during the current financial year, 2026-27.

A digital planetarium uses computer software and high-resolution digital projectors (or LED panels) to display 3D simulations of the night sky, space travel, and science visuals inside a dome theatre. Unlike traditional optical-mechanical projectors that only show fixed star positions, digital systems can fly viewers through galaxies, simulate different time periods, and play full-dome films.
Ms. Kumari was accompanied by Department Secretary Himanshu Sharma and a host of other senior officials during the press conference.

In order to generate public interest in science and technology, efforts are also being made to operate mobile science exhibition buses, observatory domes, and astro parks through the National Council of Science Museums.

Notably, the state currently has two functional planetariums—one each in Patna and Darbhanga. The planetarium in Darbhanga was established in 2023, while the renovation of the Patna planetarium has already been completed.

articles.title: Transgender persons to be roped in for tax collection in West Bengal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Minister Agnimitra Paul launches a programme to provide dignified, alternative livelihoods to trans persons

The West Bengal government will engage transgender persons to collect municipal tax and spread traffic awareness. Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul said the initiative, called “Brihannala Brigade”, will provide an opportunity for a dignified livelihood for the transpersons.

“The CM wishes that they (transgender people no) longer have to resort to begging at traffic signals; instead, we want to offer them an alternative, respectable livelihood. We have decided that those among them who are interested will receive training from the police and be deployed at traffic signals. Their role will be to sensitise the public about traffic rules and safety measures,” Ms. Paul said on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

She further added that another group of transgender persons would be trained to collect outstanding taxes, which could help address the staff shortage that leads to delayed collections and large pending amounts.

The Minister also added that each of these transgender individuals will be provided with training to engage in this work so that they can conduct better public interaction and do their work seamlessly. They will receive a stipend for the work, Ms. Paul said.

The West Bengal government has started an initiative to offer relief in paying outstanding property taxes, including in the actual sums and interest, to encourage defaulters to pay their outstanding balances.
According to Kolkata Municipal Corporation estimates, they have around ₹6800 crore outstanding property tax pending, including personal properties, mixed-use properties, and commercial properties.

In 2022, the previous Mamata Banerjee government decided to allow transgender persons to apply for government jobs under the general category to help them have better opportunities in employment. A Transgender Development Board was set up in 2017, but the board could not undertake many activities for the welfare of members of the community. The last census carried out in the state in 2011 put the number of transgender people in the state at 30,349. The actual number of people of the third gender may be higher, several groups working for the community say.

articles.title: Trinamool supporters attacked outside the police station as police questioned Abhishek
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The supporters of Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee

Supporters of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) were allegedly attacked on Friday (November 20, 2026) by supporters of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) outside a police station while party leader Abhishek Banerjee was being questioned by Kolkata Police at the Girish Park police station.

Videos of the scuffle and the assault on women supporters of the Trinamool were shared on social media and by the Mamata AITC. In the videos, groups of women alleged to be BJP supporters were seen chasing another group of women. Supporters of the Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee. The BJP leaders denied allegations of the assault but claimed that Trinamool supporters were trying to incite tensions by gathering outside the police station.

“@BJP4Bengal workers gathered outside Girish Park Police Station today, seemingly intent on harassing, heckling and assaulting our workers, did not even spare ordinary citizens and parents who had come to pick up their children from school,” the party shared on social media. The Mamata AITC leader raised questions on the role of politics.

The police complaint against the Diamond Harbour MP was filed in connection with remarks reportedly made by him on 29 October, in which he criticised sections of the police administration, alleging that officers were acting under political pressure. Mr. Banerjee took to social media to share videos of BJP leaders, including Suvendu Adhikari, alleging threats to the police when they were in the Opposition.

After the BJP came to power, several FIRs were registered against Abhishek Banerjee. He has been summoned to appear before the police on numerous occasions. Later in the day, the Trinamool leader filed a Zero FIR at Girish Park Police Station, highlighting how Suvendu Adhikari, Dilip Ghosh, and other BJP leaders threatened the Kolkata Police and the West Bengal Police on multiple occasions.

“The expertise and urgency shown by Girish Park PS in connection with Abhishek Banerjee’s matter—we hope the same expertise and urgency will be shown by them in connection with this Zero FIR, and that they will investigate the matter,” Arka Nag, an advocate representing Trinamool Congress leader, said.

articles.title: Chandel district official issues advisory after spurious liquor kills 11 in Manipur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chandel district authorities have urged the people to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor
Manipur’s Chandel district administration on Friday (November 20, 2026) issued an advisory, urging people to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor.
The public advisory followed the death of 11 people due to consumption of spurious liquor in the district’s Chakpikarong Sub-Division. The deaths have been reported since Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

According to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office, 180 others are undergoing treatment at two private hospitals in Imphal. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited these hospitals on Friday and took stock of the treatment being provided to the patients.

Advising the general public to exercise utmost caution, the district administration said the cause of the deaths was yet to be “medically and scientifically established”. It asked people to refrain from consuming locally brewed liquor or alcoholic beverages of doubtful origin, particularly from suspected sources in the affected areas.

“Any person experiencing vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, blurred vision, breathing difficulty or other unusual symptoms following alcohol consumption should immediately seek medical attention at the nearest facility,” the advisory read.
It also advised people who may have consumed liquor from the same suspected source to seek medical evaluation even if they are not experiencing symptoms.

“The public is requested to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor to the nearest police station or the concerned authorities,” the advisory further read, requesting village authorities, civil society organisations, women’s organisations and youth clubs to assist in spreading awareness.

The Manipur government partially lifted 30 years of alcohol prohibition in December 2023, although extremist groups in the State continue to target liquor businesses. Years of prohibition led to certain areas turning into local liquor dens, selling alcoholic beverages of suspect quality.
Spurious liquor has claimed lives in other northeastern States where prohibition is enforced. For instance, 23 people were killed in Nagaland’s Mokokchung and Tuensang districts about two months ago.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved maths’ greatest riddle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics

A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday (November 20, 2026) that he had used the firm’s Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.
“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpoge wrote in a four-page note released Friday (November 20, 2026).
The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.
It is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, which offers $1 million for a solution to each.
Under the institute’s rules, a solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand two years of scrutiny.
Mr. Alpoge said the method also resolves a broader version of the problem known as the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis.

He said he and Claude had produced a version of the proof in Lean, a programming language that allows mathematical arguments to be checked by a computer, and that he was releasing only that version for now.
A full written argument would be extremely long, he said, adding that he had not yet mastered all of the mathematics involved and planned to write it up properly.

Mr. Alpoge said he had consulted Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei before announcing the result and acknowledged that its timing could be viewed cynically, without elaborating, though he was probably referring to this week’s record IPO.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

fullParagraphs: Odisha Chief Minister said heavy rainfall was expected in Mayurbhanj and Balasore over the next 24 hours, with its impact likely to extend to neighbouring Jajpur, Bhadrak, Kendrapara and Jagatsinghpur districts
As many as 14 flights were cancelled at the Birsa Munda Airport in Ranchi on Saturday (November 21) due to inclement weather triggered by cyclone ‘Akvan’, an official said.
Cyclone Akvan causes 14 Ranchi airport flight cancellations due to poor visibility and bad weather.

Relief operations are underway on a war footing in Odisha’s Ganjam district after Cyclone Akvan. An ODRAF team carried out a tree-cutting operation under the Jarau Nal bridge in Chhandikendu village to clear the affected area.
Normalcy has been restored at Puri beach after Cyclone Akvan. Beach activities have resumed, bringing the shoreline back to life after the disruption caused by the cyclone.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu sought central assistance of nearly ₹100 crore for the restoration of horticultural crops damaged by cyclones Arnab and Murasu.

“Naidu has written a letter to Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Shivraj Singh Chouhan, seeking additional financial assistance for the restoration of horticulture crops damaged by two consecutive cyclones,” a press release said.
The cyclones damaged crops across 29,960 hectares in 18 districts, affecting 71,576 farmers and causing losses estimated at ₹1,092 crore, he said.

The cyclone had considerably lost its intensity when it made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha. “The cyclonic storm Akvan crossed the south coastal Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh close to Gopalpur with a wind speed of 70-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph during 7.30 a.m. to 8.30 a.m.,” said the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
Landfall of Cyclone Akvan nears Odisha and Andhra Pradesh coasts as land interaction begins, with heavy rainfall and prolonged impact anticipated.
The depression is likely to move nearly northwards over Odisha and weaken further into a low-pressure area during next 6 hours, said IMD

articles.title: Kalpakkam DAE Centre conducts emergency preparedness drive
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kalpakkam Centre of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), which houses a number of nuclear facilities, conducted a surprise emergency preparedness drive on Friday (November 20, 2026) to assess the preparedness and response capabilities of the Centre and the managements of the different plants in handling unlikely emergency situations.

This is an annual feature and is conducted as an unannounced exercise, a press release stated. More than 7,000 personnel were evacuated as part of the simulated emergency response and it was completed within 90 minutes. The exercise was held under the supervision of Kalpakkam Emergency Committee headed by S.B. Selvakumar, Station Director, MAPS.

The Kalpakkam Centre houses the Madras Atomic Power Station (MAPS), operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL); the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR); the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR), built and commissioned by BHAVINI; and the Nuclear Recycle Board.

articles.title: Break free of limiting beliefs to achieve new heights: PM Modi at IIT Kharagpur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Narendra Modi joins Platinum Jubilee celebrations of the first IIT of the country and says the institute has and will continue to play a major role in nation building

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 21, 2026) said that if people go ahead with the “nation first” mindset, then new opportunities will come their way. He asked students to break free of limiting beliefs to achieve new heights, at the Platinum jubilee celebrations of the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur.

“This place has always come forward in building the nation at every stage of the country since its independence,” Mr. Modi said while addressing the students at the 75th anniversary celebrations at IIT Kharagpur, which is also the first IIT of independent India. He also hoped that the institute will continue to make similar contributions in building the future of the nation.

“We have limiting beliefs; we limit our thoughts, our dreams, our aspirations, our talent, and give up. But we only reach our full potential if we break free of the limits to unlock new possibilities,” Mr. Modi said. He added that people put limit to their own thoughts, restricting the opportunities in their lives and of the nation.
Mr Modi said that during his tenure as the PM, he has broken the limits and achieved many such goals which people believed to be “impossible”.

“ Poverty in India was known to be a permanent problem. But there was no real change made through policy; they only made files. People took the situation for granted. But when we came to power, we changed this mentality and empowered the poor and started schemes to get them out of poverty,” Mr. Modi said. He added that according to a World Bank report, in the last 12-13 years at least 50 crore people in India have been taken out of poverty.

Mr. Modi added that in the coming days, when India is going forward towards a “Viksit Bharat”, IIT Kharagpur is sure to play a major role in building that dream. The PM further said that he hopes the 100 years of IIT Kharagpur will be celebrated in the Vikshit Bharat in the coming years.

VIDEO | Kharagpur, West Bengal: At the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur, Prime Minister Narendra Modi says, "Break the limit, unlock the possibilities. Let me share a few examples with you today. Just think, until 20 years ago, poverty was considered a permanent problem in our country. Five decades ago, slogans were raised from the Red Fort about eradicating poverty. However, whenever it came to taking action at the policy level, the entire system would simply prepare files and sit idle." (Source: Narendra Modi YT) (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd)
West Bengal Governor R.N. Ravi , Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay were among the others present at the 75-year program.

Meanwhile, the director of the institute took the stage and said that under the PM’s leadership, they are now remaining true to the mission of IIT Kharagpur. “From grassroots to skyrockets, that is the new IIT Kharagpur,” Professor Suman Chakraborty said. He also added that IIT Kharagpur alumni and Google CEO Sundar Pichai have offered a 5 million dollar support for applied Artificial Intelligence research.

Narendra Modi joins Platinum Jubilee celebrations of the first IIT of the country and says the institute has and will continue to play a major role in nation building

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 21, 2026) said that if people go ahead with the “nation first” mindset, then new opportunities will come their way. He asked students to break free of limiting beliefs to achieve new heights, at the Platinum jubilee celebrations of the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur.

“This place has always come forward in building the nation at every stage of the country since its independence,” Mr. Modi said while addressing the students at the 75th anniversary celebrations at IIT Kharagpur, which is also the first IIT of independent India. He also hoped that the institute will continue to make similar contributions in building the future of the nation.

“We have limiting beliefs; we limit our thoughts, our dreams, our aspirations, our talent, and give up. But we only reach our full potential if we break free of the limits to unlock new possibilities,” Mr. Modi said. He added that people put limit to their own thoughts, restricting the opportunities in their lives and of the nation.

Mr Modi said that during his tenure as the PM, he has broken the limits and achieved many such goals which people believed to be “impossible”.

“ Poverty in India was known to be a permanent problem. But there was no real change made through policy; they only made files. People took the situation for granted. But when we came to power, we changed this mentality and empowered the poor and started schemes to get them out of poverty,” Mr. Modi said. He added that according to a World Bank report, in the last 12-13 years at least 50 crore people in India have been taken out of poverty.

Mr. Modi added that in the coming days, when India is going forward towards a “Viksit Bharat”, IIT Kharagpur is sure to play a major role in building that dream. The PM further said that he hopes the 100 years of IIT Kharagpur will be celebrated in the Vikshit Bharat in the coming years.

Five decades ago, slogans were raised from the Red Fort about eradicating poverty. However, whenever it came to taking action at the policy level, the entire system would simply prepare files and sit idle." articles.title: Kannada writer Ravi Hanj arrested at Kochi airport amid Basava Mantapa book controversy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ravi Hanj was detained during security checks while attempting to travel abroad, say Kerala Police sources. He will be handed over to Karnataka Police

Kannada writer Ravi Hanj, who is at the centre of a major controversy over alleged derogatory remarks against 12th-century social reformer Basavanna in his book Basava Mantapa and in interviews around the book , has been detained by Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel at Cochin International Airport in Keralam.

Mr. Hanj was detained during security checks on Saturday (November 21, 2026) while attempting to travel abroad, State police sources said. He was being taken for medical examinations, the sources said.
The CISF took Mr. Hanj into custody acting on a lookout notice issued against him by the Belagavi police. He will be handed over to the Karnataka Police, sources added.
Mr. Hanj was recently booked by the police in Bengaluru, Belagavi, Bagewadi and Vijayapura following complaints alleged derogatory remarks against Basavanna and the Lingayat community.

The Karnataka Cabinet on Thursday decided to confiscate his book following complaints by Veerashiva-Lingayat groups. The book’s publisher, Vishweshwar Bhat, has also been named in the Bengaluru and Vijayapura FIRs. The book is a compilation of columns published in the Viswavani newspaper under the same title Basava Mantapa . It was released as a book in Bengaluru on November 15.

The government decided to confiscate the book following representations from Basava Samiti that alleged that the writer made the derogatory remarks in the book and in an interview published on Viswavani’s social media channels on November 13. The complaints have sought legal action against the writer, editor and others allegedly involved, and requested authorities to prevent further circulation of the book and content that could hurt religious sentiments. The BJP also demanded action against the writer.

Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara, briefing the media after Thursday’s Cabinet meeting, had said they were not banning the book but “forfeiting all copies”, and there was a provision for the same under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. However, there had been no notification from the government till November 21 afternoon to empower the police to forfeit the books.

articles.title: People will never forget BRS corruption: Telangana Congress president Mahesh Kumar Goud

fullParagraphs: Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) president and MLC Mahesh Kumar Goud claimed that people would never forget the alleged misappropriation of public money by the previous Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) government and resources given the large-scale corruption during its decade-long rule.

Speaking to the media in Nizamabad, he said several instances of corruption during the previous regime had come to light with evidence, and those responsible could not escape accountability. His response comes in the wake of BRS party’s relentless criticism of corruption charges against the Congress government.

He alleged that former Chief Minister K. Chandrashekhar Rao and former Minister T. Harish Rao were responsible for the alleged exploitation of Telangana’s water resources during the BRS regime. The Kaleshwaram project, conceived as a major irrigation initiative, had resulted in the wastage of public money worth several lakh crore rupees, he charged.

The BRS regime had also witnessed large-scale irregularities in land transactions and land-related matters, he alleged, adding that the list of alleged corruption cases under the previous government was extensive.

On inter-State water disputes, he asserted that Telangana would not surrender even a single drop of its legitimate share of water. The Congress government was committed to protecting the State’s interests and ensuring that its rightful water allocations were secured, he said.
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy was governing with determination, keeping development as the government’s principal objective, the TPCC president said.
