articles.title: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output. On the other hand, fuel-related sectors contracted again

Growth in the core industrial sectors of the economy climbed to a series-high of 10.9% in October 2026, driven by a surge in electricity generation, and coal, cement, and iron ore production, and a low base effect, official data released on Friday (November 20, 2026) showed.

Data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on the Index of Core Industries shows that growth in October surpassed the 8.2% in September, the previous series high. The new index, released this year with a base year of 2022-23, has data that goes back only up to April 2024.
However, the data also shows that the strong growth figure in October was also likely aided by the fact that the index grew a relatively poor 0.8% in October last year.

“While core output surged by 10.9% in October 2026, the fastest pace in the new series, this was supported by a low base related to the shift in the festive calendar, with output having expanded by a marginal 0.8% in the year ago month,” Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA said.

“While the growth print for October 2026 signals a strong start for the third quarter of FY2027, this is largely optical,” Ms. Nayar added. “The average performance for October-November 2026 would provide a better assessment, as this would adjust for festive base effects.”

Within the index, the coal sector saw growth accelerating to 23.05% in October 2026, far faster than the 10.7% registered in September. October’s performance, however, is likely also due to low base effect, since the sector contracted 8.4% in October last year.

The growth in the index, however, is in line with what the industry itself has reported. Coal India, the country’s largest coal company, reported that production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October.

A major reason for the growth in coal production was likely demand from the power sector, which saw electricity generation jump by 21.6% in October 2026, up from 12.6% in the previous month. However, this sector too could have benefited from a low base effect, since it contracted nearly 7% in October 2025.
Within the index, the infrastructure-related sectors were the only ones that grew strongly without the aid of a statistical low base effect.

The iron ore sector, for example, grew at a three-month high of 23.4% in October 2026, compared to 18.4% in September and 8.7% in October last year. One of the factors driving this strong growth was that steel production grew at 7.3% in October, the fastest rate in seven months.

articles.title: Russia dusts off its pre-war demands as the U.S. raises discussing European security at Ukraine talks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The proposal to discuss broader security arrangements for Europe was floated by Donald Trump’s envoys, and that has worried Ukraine and its Western allies, who fear it will play into Moscow’s hands and weaken NATO

After nearly five years of fighting in Ukraine, the Kremlin is eagerly embracing a U.S. offer to discuss post-war European security, and Moscow is using that diplomatic opening to reaffirm the tough demands that President Vladimir Putin put forward before the start of his full-scale invasion.

The proposal to discuss broader security arrangements for Europe was floated by U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys, and that has worried Ukraine and its Western allies, who fear it will play into Moscow's hands and weaken NATO.
The Kremlin strongly backed the U.S. idea, describing a review of the broader European security framework as vital for a settlement of Europe's most devastating conflict since World War II.

articles.title: Key takeaways from the Quad, ASEAN-India, and East Asia Summits in Manila | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Apart from the bilateral visits, Mr. Modi’s multilateral ASEAN engagements showed a growing desire to work more closely with the grouping at a time when global powers are working in a more unilateral manner

Prime Minister Narendra Modi took part in three back-to-back multilateral meetings on the side-lines of the annual Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) summits in Manila this week. The summits, including the ASEAN-India Summit, East Asia Summit and then the Quad Summit along with U.S. President Donald Trump, Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi and Australian PM Anthony Alabanese ended with several concrete announcements. They also sent deeper underlying message on India’s broad-basing its ‘Act East’ and Indo-Pacific policies, even as the world turned its attention to the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral later in the week.

In 2025, PM Modi had pulled out of attending the ASEAN Summits in Kuala Lumpur due to what was seen as a combination of domestic commitments around Diwali and trade friction with U.S. President Donald Trump. Ties with the Philippines have improved dramatically since President Bongbong Marcos’ visit to Delhi in August 2025, and hence it was doubly important for PM Modi to attend the two conferences hosted by him- the ASEAN- India summit, which includes Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Vietnam, as well as the East Asia Summit, which brings in U.S., Russia, China, Japan and South Korea. In addition, the invitation to the Quad Summit hosted by the U.S. and being held for the first time in Mr. Trump’s turbulent presidency was important to fit in, given concerns over his commitment to the Indo-Pacific grouping, and PM Modi ended his day with that.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: Key takeaways from the Quad, ASEAN-India, and East Asia Summits in Manila | Explained. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

articles.title: FBI, U.S. Agriculture Department breached by hackers, reports say
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The newly uncovered breaches at the FBI and USDA were described as hacks, which are different from outages like the ones that afflicted Microsoft Outlook and the Federal Aviation Administration

The FBI is investigating a ​suspected breach of a nationwide database ‌used by federal, state and ​local law enforcement agencies ⁠to share criminal justice information, CNN reported on Friday (November 20, 2026), citing two people ‌briefed on the investigation.

The apparent compromise of the National ‌Crime Information Center database would ‌mark ⁠the second intrusion involving ⁠an FBI system in recent months and the latest in a string ​of cyber incidents that ‌have alarmed U.S. officials over the past week.
The agency did not respond to a ‌request for comment from Reuters .
The ​FBI database is used by law enforcement agencies nationwide ⁠to store and share information on warrants, criminal histories and background ‌checks.
The U.S. Agriculture Department was also breached by hackers in cyberattacks, U.S. media reported on Friday.
It remains unclear whether these two incidents are related and who is responsible for them.
U.S. President Donald Trump has sought to calm the public and urged people to "relax", while officials said the various outages were not linked to criminal activity.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) told employees that a system used to facilitate payments to farmers was targeted in a cyberattack, NBC reported, citing two former USDA officials.
The hackers may use the payments system as a backdoor to access more sensitive material, the former officials told NBC.

The USDA deals with "a bunch of scary biologic issues" and "if an adversary or a competitor were to have access to that same information... they could use our own research against us," a former official was quoted as saying.

articles.title: Pakistan Climate Minister arrives in Delhi to attend SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Pakistan is the current chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) (SCO_CHS) for the period of 2026-27; the event, which will be inaugurated by PM Modi, will be held at Delhi’s iconic Purana Quila (Old Fort), a 16th Century fort built by Emperor Humayun

Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Dr. Musadik Masood Malik , arrived in Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026) for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, officials said.
Mr. Malik is representing Pakistan at a cultural meeting of the SCO in Delhi, the Pakistan High Commission in India said.
Pakistan is the current chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) (SCO_CHS) for the period of 2026-27.

The SCO is represented by China, India, Russia, Iran, Pakistan, Belarus, and Central Asian countries such as Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan. Almost all the member countries of the SCO are ancient civilisations that date back to the BCE era.

The dialogue, which will be organised by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs, was proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO leaders’ Summit in Tianjin last year and adopted by the SCO Council. According to the sources, the government has invited Pakistan’s Minister for National Heritage and Culture Aurungzeb Khan Khichi, for the event. Culture Ministers from the 10 member states, including China, Russia, Iran, Belarus and Central Asian states, 15 Dialogue partners and observer countries have been invited.

The event, which will be inaugurated by Mr. Modi, will be held at Delhi’s iconic Purana Quila (Old Fort), a 16th Century fort built by Emperor Humayun. The fort is also the site of many excavations showcasing India’s ancient past spanning nearly 3,000 years, from the Pre-Mauryan, Mauryan, Sunga, Kushana, Gupta, Post-Gupta period to medieval-era Rajput, Sultanate and Mughal periods, officials said, explaining its importance.

articles.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon taking on Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Google said the new model was built for complex coding, analytical reasoning, and enterprise workflows
Google has launched a new AI model, Gemini 4 Neon, that it said was primed for complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.
According to the company, Neon ranked ahead of comparable models, including Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Sol, on several benchmarks.
Gemini 4 Neon is priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens with a million-token context window.
Google noted that the new model was designed to support long-running agentic workflows and ensure that tasks are completed, while balancing out costs.
Meanwhile users of the Gemini app could expect better writing and knowledge work, reliable research, and faster responses when faced with challenging tasks, per the company.

“Get more done while stretching usage limits further when handing off tedious to-dos, like analysing billing statements to spot why a utility charge spiked or cross-checking multiple receipts and documents to negotiate a refund,” suggested Google in a blog post.
The search giant affirmed that its new model maintained Gemini 4 Carbon-level safeguards against severe misuse and prompt injection, and also advanced model alignment.

“Neon is built for complex coding, analytical reasoning, and production-grade enterprise workflows. While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects, and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency. Neon delivers frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently,” stated Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect at Google.

articles.title: Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.

As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

fullParagraphs: Suri: The Seventh Note by Tathvamasi Studios is set in a universe controlled by evil music. The game was launched in October

The story of Suri: The Seventh Note, a 2D video game by Bengaluru-based Tathvamasi Studios, is set in a world corrupted by an evil version of music. Everything in this universe moves in tune with that nefarious sonic presence. The protagonist, Ajira, must find a fruit located at the centre of the island to save her mother from certain death. Soon, she realises her actions shall determine the fate of the island itself.

Suri: The Seventh Note is the brainchild of Glen Martin from Kochi, founder of Tathvamasi Studios, who is also the game director of the video. He is joined by Chitrak Srivastava, co-founder and the game’s art director. The game was launched on Playstation Store and Steam in October.

Glen, formerly a data scientist, found himself immersed in game-making during the pandemic. He began by making smaller games, with friends from different places joining him on a Discord server to help. “When we started to build the game, it was not meant to be a project. But once we realised its potential, we began to think about what could be unique about this game,” says Glen.
Glen Martin and Chitrak Srivastava | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

“At that point, I was playing a parry-focused combat game called Sekiro. It’s a very hard game, and I am not good at it. But then I saw a lot of streamers play the game skilfully, without even taking a single hit, and I realised that when the game is played at that level, it has a certain rhythmic quality to it,” he adds. “The sounds of the sword clinking, the jumps and movements, everything felt choreographed.”
This ultimately led him to turn Suri… into a rhythm platformer game.

Suri... is a mix of two different games: rhythm and platformer. Rhythm games are music-themed action games that assess a player’s sense of timing and metre, while platformers are a sub-genre where a main character moves through uneven terrain and suspended platforms.

“There are very few games that have done this before, so our well of references was limited. In Suri..., the world moves to the rhythm. All the things that you would normally interact with in a regular platformer, like traps, obstacles, etc., are all tied to the rhythm in our game. You have to listen to the music to understand when a thing would move up and down or when a leaf would open or close and so on,” explains Glen. “When played well, it feels like dancing through levels.”

In 2024, Suri was one of five games at the inaugural edition of PlayStation’s India Hero Project, an incubator programme from Sony Interactive Entertainment. This ultimately allowed Glen to quit his job and hire more people.
A still from Suri: The Seventh Note | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

articles.title: CCMB team identifies genes that spur nerve repair, raise possibility of paralysis treatment
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) , Hyderabad, have identified two genes that can restore damaged nerve cells’ ability to regenerate, raising the possibility of new gene-based treatments for paralysis caused by spinal cord injuries.

The study, led by Ishwariya Venkatesh, found that activating two developmental genes, NR2F1 and NR2F6, enabled severed nerve fibres to regrow across completely injured spinal cords in mice, leading to measurable improvements in movement.

The spinal cord transmits signals from the brain to the rest of the body, enabling movement and sensation. Damage to it can cause paralysis because nerve cells in adult mammals generally lose their ability to regenerate. Despite decades of research, there is no treatment that can restore the lost neural connections.

The researchers sought to understand why young neurons can grow and regenerate while adult neurons cannot. Their investigation focused on proteins that activate growth-related genes during development but become less active as the brain matures. The team discovered that the genes NR2F1 and NR2F6, which had not previously been linked to nerve regeneration, decline by 70-80% in adult brains.

Restoring either gene in adult mice prompted damaged nerve fibres to regenerate across the injury site and extend beyond it. Untreated animals, by contrast, showed little or no regrowth. The treated mice also showed improved mobility, including better hind-limb movement and grip strength. Recovery became evident about five weeks after the injury and continued thereafter.

The two genes, however, triggered regeneration through different mechanisms. NR2F1 activated genes involved in remodelling DNA and rebuilding cellular structures needed for growth. NR2F6, meanwhile, suppressed several routine cellular activities, allowing neurons to redirect resources towards repairing damaged nerve fibres.

The team also found that NR2F6 reorganises the three-dimensional structure of DNA in injured neurons, bringing growth-related genes closer to the regulatory elements that control their activity. Researchers said this was the first evidence linking large-scale genome reorganisation to nerve regeneration in the brain or spinal cord.

Published in The EMBO Journal , the study is still at the preclinical stage. The genes were delivered before the injury in mice, and the recovery was partial. The findings, however, offer a potential framework for developing gene-based therapies to repair spinal cord damage, said a press release.

articles.title: Raichur is a treasure trove of Kannada literature, says Rajappa Dalawai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Raichur is a rich repository of Kannada literature and culture, having produced several eminent writers who have made significant contributions to the literary world, said Rajappa Dalawai, chairperson of the State-level Selection Committee of the Department of Public Libraries, Bengaluru.

Speaking at the 71st Karnataka Rajyotsava celebrations organised at the Adikavi Sri Maharshi Valmiki University in Raichur on Friday, he said Kannada was not merely a medium of communication but also a symbol of the State’s culture and identity. Writers such as Channanna Walikar and Shantarasa, who transformed the course of Kannada literature, hailed from Raichur, he noted.

Referring to the rich literary heritage of Kannada, he said the language had won eight Jnanpith Awards and had been accorded classical language status in recognition of its antiquity and literary tradition. The recent Booker Prize recognition for a work by Banu Mushtaq was another achievement for Kannada literature, he said.

Pointing out that Kannada had been among the first Indian languages to be incorporated into computer technology and ATMs, he urged students to cultivate the habit of reading books rather than spending excessive time on mobile phones and social media reels.

Senior writer from Raichur and Rajyotsava awardee Veera Hanuman said the real architects of literature were often the ancestors and folk artistes who had created and preserved literary traditions despite not having formal education.

Razak Ustad, newly appointed member of the Karnataka State Higher Education Council, expressed concern that Kalyana Karnataka, despite having fertile land, 10 rivers and abundant natural resources, continued to lag behind other regions in per capita income. Regional disparities persisted even seven decades after the unification of Karnataka, he said, urging people to develop the habit of questioning and undertake introspection.

Presiding over the programme, Vice-Chancellor of the university Shivanand Kelaginamani said writers, artistes and activists who had worked for the development of Kannada should be remembered. He said the benefits of Article 371(J) should extend beyond government employment and reach the private sector and industries as well, creating more job opportunities for local people.
University Registrar A. Chennappa said the people of Raichur should recognise and build upon the region’s rich cultural, literary, artistic and agricultural resources.
Evaluation Registrar Virupakshaiah D.B.M., Finance Officer Latha M.S., deans, faculty members, representatives of academic associations, teaching and non-teaching staff and students were present.

articles.title: Dharwad to host State-level 10K cross-country run on Nov. 29
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The District Olympics Association is organising the event as part of the Rajyotsava celebrations
The District Olympics Association will organise a State-level 10K cross-country run in Dharwad on November 29 as part of the Rajyotsava celebrations.

Announcing this at a press conference on Thursday, association president Shivu Hiremath said that the event is being organised jointly with the Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation and the Department of Youth Empowerment and Sports.
The competition will feature separate 10-km races for men and women, held in memory of late S.S. Agadi, a retired Sports Authority of India coach, and late athlete Kallavva Sindhogi, respectively.

articles.title: Taj Yelahanka, Tata Group’s 400th hotel, opens in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL), the hospitality arm of the Tata Group, founded by Jamsetji Tata, has opened its 400th hotel property, Taj Yelahanka, in Bengaluru. Tata’s maiden hotel venture, The Taj Mahal Palace in Mumbai (then Bombay), opened in 1903.

The new 256-key property was built in partnership with Krishna GVK Luxury Hotels Limited, formerly known as Taj GVK Hotels & Resorts. This is the seventh joint project between the two companies and marks Krishna GVK Luxury Hotels’ entry into the Bengaluru market.

Speaking to the media at the launch, Puneet Chhatwal, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of IHCL, said that with this new property, the group was expanding its footprint in rapidly developing north Bengaluru. Krishna Bhupal, Joint Managing Director of Krishna G.V.K. Luxury Hotels, said the company aims to expand its overall hospitality inventory beyond 2,200 keys across Indian markets through both organic development and acquisitions.

articles.title: Amid cold wave, students’ indefinite strike against J&K recruitment board scam gathers steam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Protesting government job aspirants on Saturday (November 21, 2026) launched an indefinite strike in Srinagar amid a cold wave over the government’s failure to act against the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB), the main recruitment agency of J&K that has become mired in a cheating scam that has led to 16 arrests so far.

While former Member of Parliament (MP) Aga Syed Ruhullah joined the protesters in Srinagar, other regional parties also demanded the cancellation of all examinations held by the Board and called for “fixing the responsibility”.
Speaking at the Sher-i-Kashmir Park, Mr. Ruhullah said the protest is a “rare effort to open up space where youth could fight for their rights”.

“We demand that heads must roll. We have the elected government and an unelected government ruling J&K. Both share responsibility for it. Unfortunately, there is a sense of complacency. The examinations should be postponed, responsibility for the irregularities fixed and reforms carried out. The administration should engage students and address their concerns,” said Mr. Ruhullah.

Mr. Ruhullah joined scores of students and aspirants who held a sit-in all day in Srinagar. With evening temperature dipping, a spokesman of Mr. Ruhullah said, “There was no food or blankets. No entry. Students on a peaceful sit-in are being frozen out on a bitter Srinagar night. Their only crime is asking for justice over the alleged Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) recruitment rigging.”
The night temperature has dipped to around zero degrees Celsius in Srinagar amid a severe cold wave.
On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts.

Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. Besides 16 arrests made in the case, the police said it filed three First Information Reports (FIRs) and recovered eight wireless devices, 22 mobile phones and four vehicles of the accused.

However, Board chairman Shrikant Balasaheb Suse said the “examination was not compromised by a paper leak or mass malpractice” and announced that the upcoming exams will be held “as per the schedule”.
Facing a growing public outcry, J&K Education Minister Shamim Firdous said strict action should be taken “if any irregularities or rigging are found”.

The three main accused, Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, P.V. Kulkarni and Manisha Sanjay Havaldar, were public servants as they were engaged by the National Testing Agency (NTA), and had procured confidential questions illegally in conspiracy with the co-accused, the court had said.

The trial will begin on a day-to-day basis from November 25, 2026.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) had earlier filed a chargesheet against 13 accused in a fast-track court dealing with criminal cases arising from paper leaks and the use of other unfair means in public examinations.
It also filed a supplementary chargesheet against the 14th accused, Sheshrao Suryawanshi alias Raj Suryawanshi, a resident of Nanded in Maharashtra, who was arrested on September 2, 2026.

In a statement here on Saturday, he said those responsible for the tragedy must face immediate, strict action, and the affected families should receive full support and fair compensation without delay.

“The news of several people dying from toxic liquor in Manipur is deeply saddening. I express my deepest condolences to the bereaved families and hope for the patients’ speedy recovery. This is not an accident, but the result of the BJP government’s negligence. First, violence devastated hundreds of homes; now toxic liquor is wreaking havoc — the government is still asleep,” Mr. Gandhi said.
Manipur police had said that at least 16 people have died, and about 600 have been hospitalised allegedly after consuming spurious liquor in Chandel district since November 18.

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

“India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

“India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.

The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

fullParagraphs: Afterwards, meals of cooked rice were scattered around the vehicle, which was partially covered in the blood of the victims of the attack

An Israeli strike killed three Palestinians ​in a vehicle carrying papers and food for the World ⁠Central Kitchen charity in Gaza City on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Gaza's Health Ministry and witnesses said.
World Central Kitchen, an aid organisation that distributes food in the Gaza Strip, said, however, ‌that the vehicle was not affiliated with it.

The Israeli military said several militants had been targeted in the area without providing ‌further details. It did not immediately respond to questions on why ‌it ⁠had hit a vehicle that appeared to be distributing aid.
A ⁠Reuters witness said the vehicle appeared to be carrying packaged foodstuffs, and that papers inside carried World Central Kitchen's logo.
"It was just about to stop to distribute the food and ​drink to children when it was ‌hit by a missile," said Abu Zein Al-Daya, who witnessed the strike.
Afterwards, meals of cooked rice were scattered around the vehicle, which was partially covered in the blood of the victims of the attack.
The Israeli military killed seven World Central Kitchen workers ​in a 2024 strike, including citizens of Australia, Britain and Poland.
At the time, the military said there had been "serious errors and ⁠breaches of procedure" but in 2026 it said it had found no basis on which to open criminal investigations into the incident.
Israel briefly launched a ‌ground operation in Gaza earlier this week and killed six people in a strike on a hospital that it said was targeting a commander for the Palestinian militant group Hamas.
An October 2025 U.S.-backed ceasefire halted major fighting in the shattered territory but has not stopped Israeli attacks on Gaza or secured Hamas' disarmament.

"The situation poses no danger to other maritime traffic... Preparations for potential rescue operations are being made in cooperation with other authorities in Finland and internationally," the Finnish Border Guard said in a statement.
Drozdenko also said 80 drones had been shot down over the Leningrad region and lifted a drone ‌threat warning.

articles.title: States agree to UN talks aiming to regulate 'killer robots' by 2028
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Around 100 ⁠countries backed this position, but big arms-producing nations like the U.S., Russia, and Israel opposed this, resulting in a watered-down agreement that left open the question of whether future ​measures would be legally ‌binding

⁠UN talks on regulating weapons with little or no human oversight ended on Saturday (November 21, 2026) with a pledge for further discussions to develop new rules within two years, ‌an outcome weakened by Russia's opposition and disappointing human rights groups.

Proponents had called for legally binding rules within ‌a short timeframe to regulate weapons systems that can identify and engage ‌targets ⁠with varying degrees of autonomy, sometimes called "killer robots".

Around 100 ⁠countries backed this position, but big arms-producing nations like the U.S., Russia, and Israel opposed this, resulting in a watered-down agreement that left open the question of whether future ​measures would be legally ‌binding.

The member states of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons had been meeting in Geneva since Monday (November 16, 2026) as alarm grows over the use of lethal autonomous weapons systems in conflicts, including in Ukraine, ‌Sudan and West Asia.
The UN secretary-general, the pope ​and the Red Cross have all called for strong and legally binding rules.
The meeting's Swiss chair, Julien Thoeni, ⁠hailed the deal as a significant achievement for humanitarian disarmament after more than 10 years of talks.
“It shows that even in today’s deeply divided ‌world, multilateral diplomacy can still deliver concrete results," he told reporters in a hoarse voice as talks concluded after 4 a.m.
A diplomat involved in the talks from a country supporting new laws said the outcome was "disappointing but could have been much worse".
Negotiators spent hours wrangling over a handful of words overnight, diplomats said, after Russian ‌objections to rules of procedure forced the cancellation of some formal meetings.
Many rights ​groups criticised the outcome, which they said means technology now has a chance to overtake diplomacy.

articles.title: U.S. court dispatches summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun case
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Indian Code of Civil Procedure permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts designated by notification of the Central Government of India to be transmitted to Indian courts and served as though issued by those courts

A U.S. court has dispatched summonses to National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) Director Samant Goel to be served through Indian courts in connection with a case involving an alleged murder plot against Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.

articles.title: COP31 extends into overtime in Turkiye meeting
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The inability to reach compromise — every clause of the final text must be agreed upon by every participant country — is due to the familiar division between a bloc of European countries, and developing countries over a timeline to phase out fossil fuels

Much like the 1.5 degree Celsius warming ceiling, COP31 proceedings under way at Antalya in Turkiye also breached upper limits with countries, as of Saturday (November 21, 2026) evening, yet to behold a final text or convene a final plenary meeting to decide on the path forward for climate action.

Proceedings were expected to officially conclude on Friday (November 20, 2026), though historically it almost always goes into overtime and extends into the early hours of the weekend. The inability to reach a compromise — every clause of the final text must be agreed upon by every participating country — is due to the familiar division between a bloc of European countries and developing countries over a timeline to phase out fossil fuels and defining and paying out the trillions of dollars necessary to fund that transition as well as adapt to ongoing climate change.

The latest public iteration of the COP31 draft cover text, as of November 19, has eliminated references to fossil fuels phase out and net zero dates but has also deleted references to a firm US $120 billion adaptation-finance target that developing countries have been asking for as “legally binding financial obligations” on developed countries.

Taking off from the previous editions of the COP in Baku, Azerbaijan and Belem, Brazil, developed nations said they would “take the lead” in contributing at least $300 billion annually towards mitigation and adaptation to climate change by 2035, though developing countries say this should be at least $ 1.3 trillion.

Other than the thorny debate on whether loans, grants, and for-profit investments in green projects are all included in this number, there is also debate on how much of the annual money should be split between adaptation and mitigation. The $120 billion was a proposal but that now has disappeared from the latest version of the text.
This suggests that the most ambitious demands of both the developed and developing country blocs have been eliminated.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome it needs the consensus of all Parties. The Presidency has said earlier drafts were not meant to reflect consensus.

However, a widely expected outcome of raising electricity’s share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035 and scaling up the use of carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS) technologies. The latter involves unproven, expensive technology to extract atmospheric carbon dioxide. Proponents say this is necessary to counter the effects of the carbon that’s already in the atmosphere and responsible for the 1.5C temperature breach that has already occurred. To reiterate, the Paris Agreement goal is to keep temperatures below 2C and “as far as possible” below 1.5C. However, this has also been criticised by several civil society organisations as being an excuse to delay fossil-fuel phaseout.

“CC[U]S has been researched and developed for decades yet has achieved no discernible breakthroughs in efficiency, capture rates, or costs. Indeed, costs are getting higher. CCS is a tax on energy supplies at a time when affordability is strained and demand growth is seeking efficient supplies,” said Grant Hauber, Strategic Energy Finance Advisor, Asia, Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) in a statement,” CO2 capture and disposal are a pure cost to the energy and production system.”

“We’re down to the wire at COP31, and the latest texts are alarmingly far from ambitious or equitable,” said Rachel Cleetus, Climate Program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS), in a statement. “ Rich nations, most notably the EU nations, are still holding a harsh line against committing to tripling adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035. Instead of reaching agreement on urgently needed climate finance, some countries seem willing to push negotiations toward failure.”

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 21 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

📰 COP31 extends into overtime in Turkiye meeting

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The inability to reach compromise — every clause of the final text must be agreed upon by every participant country — is due to the familiar division between a bloc of European countries, and developing countries over a timeline to phase out fossil fuels

Much like the 1.5 degree Celsius warming ceiling, COP31 proceedings under way at Antalya in Turkiye also breached upper limits with countries, as of Saturday (November 21, 2026) evening, yet to behold a final text or convene a final plenary meeting to decide on the path forward for climate action.

Proceedings were expected to officially conclude on Friday (November 20, 2026), though historically it almost always goes into overtime and extends into the early hours of the weekend. The inability to reach a compromise — every clause of the final text must be agreed upon by every participating country — is due to the familiar division between a bloc of European countries and developing countries over a timeline to phase out fossil fuels and defining and paying out the trillions of dollars necessary to fund that transition as well as adapt to ongoing climate change.

The latest public iteration of the COP31 draft cover text, as of November 19, has eliminated references to fossil fuels phase out and net zero dates but has also deleted references to a firm US $120 billion adaptation-finance target that developing countries have been asking for as “legally binding financial obligations” on developed countries.

Taking off from the previous editions of the COP in Baku, Azerbaijan and Belem, Brazil, developed nations said they would “take the lead” in contributing at least $300 billion annually towards mitigation and adaptation to climate change by 2035, though developing countries say this should be at least $ 1.3 trillion.

Other than the thorny debate on whether loans, grants, and for-profit investments in green projects are all included in this number, there is also debate on how much of the annual money should be split between adaptation and mitigation. The $120 billion was a proposal but that now has disappeared from the latest version of the text.

This suggests that the most ambitious demands of both the developed and developing country blocs have been eliminated.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome it needs the consensus of all Parties. The Presidency has said earlier drafts were not meant to reflect consensus.

However, a widely expected outcome of raising electricity’s share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035 and scaling up the use of carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS) technologies. The latter involves unproven, expensive technology to extract atmospheric carbon dioxide. Proponents say this is necessary to counter the effects of the carbon that’s already in the atmosphere and responsible for the 1.5C temperature breach that has already occurred. To reiterate, the Paris Agreement goal is to keep temperatures below 2C and “as far as possible” below 1.5C. However, this has also been criticised by several civil society organisations as being an excuse to delay fossil-fuel phaseout.

“CC[U]S has been researched and developed for decades yet has achieved no discernible breakthroughs in efficiency, capture rates, or costs. Indeed, costs are getting higher. CCS is a tax on energy supplies at a time when affordability is strained and demand growth is seeking efficient supplies,” said Grant Hauber, Strategic Energy Finance Advisor, Asia, Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) in a statement,” CO2 capture and disposal are a pure cost to the energy and production system.”

“We’re down to the wire at COP31, and the latest texts are alarmingly far from ambitious or equitable,” said Rachel Cleetus, Climate Program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS), in a statement. “ Rich nations, most notably the EU nations, are still holding a harsh line against committing to tripling adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035. Instead of reaching agreement on urgently needed climate finance, some countries seem willing to push negotiations toward failure.”

articles.title: HPV vaccination: one crore doses administered in nine months
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Nearly 87% of its annual target cohort of 14-year-old girls has been covered under the national cervical cancer prevention campaign. Uttar Pradesh leads with more than 29.33 lakh girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar (13.70 lakh) and Gujarat (7.75 lakh)

India has administered more than one crore doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in less than nine months, covering nearly 87% of its annual target cohort of 14-year-old girls under the national cervical cancer prevention campaign launched in February 2026, noted a release issued by the Union Health Ministry on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

It added that Uttar Pradesh leads with more than 29.33 lakh girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar (13.70 lakh) and Gujarat (7.75 lakh). Six States — Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar — have achieved 100% coverage of their identified target populations.

The government provides the single-dose vaccine free of cost and voluntarily to eligible girls at designated government health facilities, with parental consent. The U-WIN digital platform facilitates beneficiary tracking, real-time monitoring, slot booking and digital certificates. Vaccination sessions are conducted under medical supervision, with arrangements for managing adverse events following immunisation, the Ministry said.
Among other high-performing States, Assam has recorded 95.63% coverage, followed by Telangana (95.28%), Karnataka (93.16%) and Uttarakhand (90.17%).

Chhattisgarh (86.21%) and Rajasthan (85.23%) have crossed the 80% coverage mark, while Kerala (77.02%), Tamil Nadu (76.12%), Odisha (74.90%) and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (72.99%) have achieved more than 70% coverage.

In terms of absolute numbers, Uttar Pradesh leads the country with more than 29.33 lakh 14-year-old girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar with more than 13.70 lakh and Gujarat with more than 7.75 lakh girls vaccinated.

“School teachers, Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs) and other frontline healthcare workers have worked closely with parents and communities to encourage informed participation and counter misinformation,’’ the Ministry added.

It stated that digital health infrastructure has been an important enabler of the nationwide campaign, with the U-WIN platform supporting real-time monitoring, beneficiary tracking and digital vaccination records.

The platform also enables parents to book HPV vaccination slots for their daughters and download digital vaccination certificates, making the vaccination process more accessible, convenient and transparent.

articles.title: At least 13 dead after consuming spurious liquor, over 300 hospitalised in Manipur

fullParagraphs: Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications

At least 13 people have died, and more than 300 have been hospitalised since November 18 after they consumed spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel district, police said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
The patients are mostly from Chakpikarong and surrounding areas and have been hospitalised across multiple healthcare facilities in Imphal, including JNIMS, RIMS, Shija and Babina Hospital.

"Thirteen people have been reported dead till 9 p.m. on Friday, while 346 patients have been admitted to hospitals due to suspected methanol poisoning, as they consumed spurious liquor," an official told PTI .
Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited Shija Hospital and Babina Hospital on Friday afternoon (November 20, 2026) to assess the situation and meet patients undergoing treatment.

In a social media post, Mr. Singh said, "Visited Shija Hospital at Lamphelpat, and Babina Hospital at Sajiwa, today [on Friday] to enquire about the health condition of the persons undergoing treatment after consuming spurious liquor from Chakpikarong area in Chandel District."
The Chandel district administration has intensified emergency response measures, and a team has been constituted for coordinated monitoring of the situation, an official notification said.
Four rapid response teams, equipped with adequate medicines and oxygen supplies, have been deployed in the district, the official said.

"Over 140 patients were admitted to Shija Hospital and over 41 patients at Babina Hospital. The death toll has touched 11 during the last 48 hours. The patients are undergoing medical evaluation and treatment under the close supervision of the doctors," he said.

"A medical team, led by a Specialist in General Medicine, along with essential medicines, has left for Chandel District to strengthen on-ground treatment and response", he said adding, "The government will conduct an enquiry and the culprits will be punished."
Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan .K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications.

articles.title: South Korea confirms first case of cholera in 10 years
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: It is the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001
South Korea on Friday reported its first case of cholera in 10 years, with health authorities urging people to take precautionary measures, use only safe water and wash their food properly.

The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency said health workers confirmed cholera from test samples of a person who had visited a hospital emergency room in the southeastern port city of Changwon earlier this month, showing symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea.

The agency said the unidentified person, who recovered and was discharged on Tuesday, had not travelled overseas in the past two months. It said health workers were trying to trace the source of infection and the people the person had been in contact with.

It was the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001.

The agency issued guidance urging people to stick to safe water and cooked food and to wash and peel fruits and vegetables. It also urged medical facilities to promptly test and report suspected cases.

articles.title: Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in DR Congo next week: WHO
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO

Two potential vaccines against the deadly Ebola strain gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo are set to enter trials in the outbreak's epicentre next week, the World Health Organisation announced earlier this week.
There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the explosive outbreak declared in May, triggering an international public health emergency.
A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO.

"We expect two candidate vaccines developed specifically for Bundibugyo virus to begin testing as early as next week," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told a press conference at the UN health agency's headquarters in Geneva.

The so-called Tumaini trial in the DRC is a single framework that can test the safety, efficacy and ability to trigger an immune response of multiple vaccines. The trial uses ring vaccination: immunising contacts deemed to be at high risk of infection.

Ervebo, a vaccine already approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, kicked off the Tumaini trial on October 23, at the full-scale Phase 3 level, to determine if it also offers any protection against Bundibugyo.
The trial will now also incorporate the two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which have both gone through earlier-stage, smaller-scale Phase 1 clinical trials.

One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab developed by the University of Oxford; the other, mRNA-1469, was developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Meg Doherty, head of the WHO's science for health department, said Phase 2 clinical trials with the candidate vaccines are scheduled to begin on November 26 or 27 in Bunia, the capital of the DRC's northeastern Ituri province at the epicentre of the outbreak.
If the safety and immune response data from the Phase 2 trial pass the next stage of review, the candidate jabs can move forward to a full-scale Phase 3 trial.

A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO

Two potential vaccines against the deadly Ebola strain gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo are set to enter trials in the outbreak's epicentre next week, the World Health Organisation announced earlier this week.

There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the explosive outbreak declared in May, triggering an international public health emergency.

A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO.

"We expect two candidate vaccines developed specifically for Bundibugyo virus to begin testing as early as next week," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told a press conference at the UN health agency's headquarters in Geneva.

The so-called Tumaini trial in the DRC is a single framework that can test the safety, efficacy and ability to trigger an immune response of multiple vaccines. The trial uses ring vaccination: immunising contacts deemed to be at high risk of infection.

Ervebo, a vaccine already approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, kicked off the Tumaini trial on October 23, at the full-scale Phase 3 level, to determine if it also offers any protection against Bundibugyo.

The trial will now also incorporate the two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which have both gone through earlier-stage, smaller-scale Phase 1 clinical trials.

One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab developed by the University of Oxford; the other, mRNA-1469, was developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Meg Doherty, head of the WHO's science for health department, said Phase 2 clinical trials with the candidate vaccines are scheduled to begin on November 26 or 27 in Bunia, the capital of the DRC's northeastern Ituri province at the epicentre of the outbreak.

If the safety and immune response data from the Phase 2 trial pass the next stage of review, the candidate jabs can move forward to a full-scale Phase 3 trial.

articles.title: The Rohingya | Vindication for a persecuted people
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The International Court of Justice’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide during its 2017 ‘clearance operations’ offers a measure of justice for the ethnic and religious minority, but the court has no means of enforcing its judgment

In a first of a kind ruling, the International Court of Justice held on November 19 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State during the military’s “clearance operations” in 2017. This was the first time the ICJ found a state responsible for committing genocide. Nine judges against six voted in favour of the ruling, in a case brought in 2019 by The Gambia.

The court also found that Myanmar failed to prevent genocide by civilians who joined its forces, failed to punish the perpetrators, never enacted the laws that the Genocide Convention requires, and destroyed evidence in breach of the court’s 2020 interim order. It also rejected, by 14 votes to one, the charge that Myanmar directly and publicly incited private persons to commit genocide, but declined to order citizenship for the Rohingya.

The judgment holds the state of Myanmar to account but does not convict any individual. It is final and cannot be appealed. The court ordered Myanmar to investigate and, if warranted, prosecute those responsible, guarantee that the violations will not recur, allow the “safe, voluntary and dignified” return of the displaced, restore their property and compensate the Rohingya. The amount of compensation is to be fixed later, after Myanmar reports back to the court within two years.

The Rohingya are a predominantly Muslim people who speak an Indo-Aryan language close to the Chittagonian dialect. The 2014 Census in Myanmar estimated over a million Rohingya in the country, concentrated in Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung along the Bangladesh border. Muslims have lived in Rakhine or Arakan from the time of the Mrauk U kingdom (15th to 18th century). In 1799, the British physician Francis Buchanan recorded that Muslims “long settled in Arakan” called themselves the “Rooinga”.

Many joined them, coming from Chittagong during colonial rule. Historian Jacques Leider has said the “Rohingya” took on a political and ethnic meaning in the late 1950s, when Muslim leaders adopted it to claim the status of a “national race”. In 1961, Brig. Aung Gyi of the Burmese Army publicly accepted them as an ethnic group. But this was before the coup by General Ne Win in 1962 which heralded decades of rule by the military junta in the country.

articles.title: Sri Lanka's organised crime bill gets Supreme Court nod
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality

Sri Lanka's proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill has received the Supreme Court's nod, which ruled that its provisions are "not inconsistent" with the Constitution, Speaker Jagath Wickremaratna told Parliament on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

The Bill, tabled in Parliament on October 20, has drawn criticism from local and international rights groups concerned that its provisions could undermine fundamental rights and grant sweeping powers to law enforcement agencies.

In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality.
The Speaker on Saturday (November 21, 2026) confirmed the Supreme Court's nod for the Bill and listed the clauses it directed Parliament to amend.

"The clauses in the Bill are not inconsistent with the Constitution and may be passed by a simple majority of Parliament, subject to making the amendment at the committee stage," Mr. Wickremaratna said.
He said Clause 6, which allowed the prosecution of an individual who is not a member of a criminal gang, should be deleted, citing the Court's directions.

Criticism of the Bill has centred on its broad definition of organised crime and provisions that could allow authorities to identify individuals as gang members based on their appearance or associations.

Sri Lanka's Human Rights Commission called for the Bill's withdrawal, while the Bar Association of Sri Lanka raised concerns about its impact on fundamental rights and safeguards for judicial oversight.

Rights body Amnesty International also called for its complete withdrawal, while the New York-based Human Rights Watch said the proposed legislation fell short of international human rights standards.

Rights groups have also raised concerns over extended detention, the admissibility of confessions made to senior police officers, restrictions on bail, police surveillance and searches and arrests without warrants.

articles.title: Yemen's Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on November 20
Yemen's Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday (November 21, 2026), after vowing reprisals for a "special operation" by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them.

Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was "under a hostile aerial threat".
The coalition later said it had "intercepted and destroyed" three Houthi ballistic missiles headed for the capital.
The Iran-backed Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh.
The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on Friday (November 20, 2026).
The "special operation" hit smuggling and weapons-transporting operations in Hodeida, the coalition said.
It also involved attacks on Sanaa, Saada and Taiz governorates, marking an uptick in violence after months of hostilities.

The Houthis had vowed to hit the Saudi city of Jeddah and other Red Sea ports if Hodeida was attacked, while warning airlines that Saudi airspace was "unsafe". The group also threatened Riyadh's financial district and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said its forces had "targeted operational capabilities at Hodeida port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles".

Yemen's Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday (November 21, 2026), after vowing reprisals for a "special operation" by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them.

Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.

An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was "under a hostile aerial threat".

The coalition later said it had "intercepted and destroyed" three Houthi ballistic missiles headed for the capital.

The Iran-backed Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh.

The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on Friday (November 20, 2026).

The "special operation" hit smuggling and weapons-transporting operations in Hodeida, the coalition said.

It also involved attacks on Sanaa, Saada and Taiz governorates, marking an uptick in violence after months of hostilities.

The Houthis had vowed to hit the Saudi city of Jeddah and other Red Sea ports if Hodeida was attacked, while warning airlines that Saudi airspace was "unsafe". The group also threatened Riyadh's financial district and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq.

articles.title: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.
Editorial Context: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

optsEn: Core accountability: On core sector performance
optsHi: Core accountability: On core sector performance
optsMr: Core accountability: On core sector performance
dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: Core accountability: On core sector performance. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.
